subject: Dedicated capacity: annual prepay + flexible ramp / credit exchange
messages:
From: Anya Li <anya.li@vectra.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing + payment options

Thanks for the call earlier. We're excited about Redwood's performance numbers, but the finance team is pressing on predictability. Before we escalate to procurement I wanted to confirm two things so I can give them a clean summary:

1) If we do a 2-year annual prepay, what level of term discount do you guarantee vs month-to-month?
2) We need flexibility in the first 12 months — can committed capacity be ramped in tranches and any unused prepay convert to credits rather than being lost?

Attached a simple table (vectra_ramp_matrix.xlsx) with our expected quarter-by-quarter TPU/GPU profile. Happy to jump back on a call.

—Anya
Anya Li | Head of Platform Partnerships | Vectra AI
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Li <anya.li@vectra.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02T12:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing + payment options

Thanks Anya — appreciate the table. High level answer up front: yes on phased ramps; yes on credits for unused prepaid capacity within a defined runway. Key points (summary):

- Term discounts: 12% for 1-year annual prepay, 20% for 2-year annual prepay, 26% for 3-year prepay (applies to committed baseline spend).
- Ramp flexibility: We support a phased onramp with quarterly carve-ins. You can set the committed baseline per quarter (so Year 1 can be 0/25/50/100% of baseline depending on Qs).
- Credit option: Unused prepaid capacity can be converted to refundable credits usable against Redwood API and Dedicated over a 12-month credit window. We do not do cash refunds except in special exec-approved cases.
- Credit exchange: For multi-year deals we offer a credit-refresh at year boundaries — unused Year 1 credits can roll into Year 2 but at a 90% face value (to account for pricing improvement and capacity planning).

I'm looping Marcus for the detailed pricing schedule and Karthik for legal/billing constraints. I'll attach a tailored proposal (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf) with a sample three-year tranche schedule based on your matrix.

Next steps: Marcus to propose a quarterly ramp schedule + amortized invoice plan. If that looks good we can prep a term sheet for procurement.

Best,
Tessa Morgan | Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0138
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Li <anya.li@vectra.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing schedule proposal

Anya — attaching the quick pricing snapshot below (also in attached proposal). I tried to reflect conservative ramping. Two options: standard annuitized billing vs accelerated prepay. Numbers are illustrative; I'll convert to line items if you want.

Option A — 2-year annual prepay (preferred for price):
- Year 1 committed baseline: 40 GPUs equivalent (Q1 0 / Q2 10 / Q3 15 / Q4 15)
- Year 2 committed baseline: 80 GPUs equivalent (Q1 20 / Q2 20 / Q3 20 / Q4 20)
- Effective term discount: 20% off list for committed baseline spend
- Billing: Yearly invoice at contract anniversary (prepay). Unused credits: convertible to account credits valid 12 months.

Option B — 3-year blended ramp with credit refresh (lower unit price, more aggressive ramp):
- Year 1: 30 GPUs baseline (Q1 0 / Q2 10 / Q3 10 / Q4 10)
- Year 2: 70 GPUs baseline
- Year 3: 120 GPUs baseline
- Effective term discount: 26%
- Credit roll: unused Year 1 credits roll to Year 2 at 90% value, Year 2 -> Year 3 at 95% if elected at renewal.

Billing notes:
- We can amortize prepay for internal accounting (monthly revenue recognition) while issuing single annual invoice.
- If Vectra needs quarterly invoices for AP, we can produce 4 invoices pro-rated against the annual prepay but payment terms remain prepay.

Open items for procurement/legal:
- Credit convertibility limits (we typically cap credit conversion to 30% of annual committed spend to avoid arbitrage).
- Early termination compensation: standard schedule applies unless exec-negotiated.

If you want, we can prepare a one-page mutual action plan that maps milestones (engineering onboarding, perf gates, capacity carve-outs) to the quarterly ramp.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin | Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Anya Li <anya.li@vectra.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vectra.ai
Date: 2025-09-04T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing schedule proposal

This is helpful — thanks. A couple of clarifications/asks from our side before we take this to procurement:

- Can you drop the Year 1 commitment floor to 25 GPUs for Option A but keep Year 2 at 80 GPUs, and keep the 20% discount? Our product launch timing likely shifts some Q2 demand into Q3.
- We need credit convertibility to apply to Dedicated only (we don't want credits used on hosted API). Is that possible?
- For accounting, our CFO prefers quarterly invoices tied to milestones rather than a single big prepay invoice. We appreciate the amortization note — can Redwood supply quarterly invoices with the same prepayment economic (i.e., invoices are due at each quarter start and total equals agreed annual prepay)?

If you can confirm these 3 items we'll draft a short term sheet and run it through procurement next week.

—Anya
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Li <anya.li@vectra.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-09T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — pricing schedule proposal

Anya — quick confirm from legal/billing: all three asks are doable with the following clarifications that we'll include in the term sheet:

1) Year 1 floor: we can set Year 1 committed baseline to 25 GPUs for Option A and preserve the 20% term discount (will be reflected in the annualized committed spend).
2) Credit scoping: credits can be restricted to Dedicated capacity only; we'll add an explicit clause limiting redemption to Dedicated SKUs.
3) Quarterly invoicing: we can emit four pro-rated invoices due at the start of each quarter that together equal the annual prepay amount. In the agreement we'll label the invoices as "advance/commit installments" and maintain prepay semantics (i.e., the committed spend is prepaid).

Additional items to expect in the term sheet:
- Credit conversion cap: 30% of annual committed spend (to prevent cross-product arbitrage).
- Credit refund: no cash refunds; credits only unless exception approved by exec.
- Roll mechanics: unused credits roll forward per Marcus' schedule (90% face value from Y1->Y2).
- Service-level onboarding gate: production ramp beyond Q3 requires passing the staging perf gate (latency and throughput targets).

If that all looks good I'll draft the short term sheet and circulate for signatures. Tessa — please attach the updated schedule and we can time a procurement walkthrough on Monday.

Karthik Iyer | Head of Contracts & Billing | Redwood Inference
